title: Possible prescribing cascade: {index} → ankle swelling → {marker}
plain: Amlodipine-type blood-pressure medicines can lead to ankle swelling, and a water pill started for that swelling often helps little while adding its own effects.
clinician: Dihydropyridine CCB edema is driven by arteriolar vasodilation and responds poorly to diuretics; new loop diuretic dispensing after CCB initiation is a documented cascade (Savage 2020).
question: Could the ankle swelling be linked to {index}, and is {marker} still the best way to manage it?

title: Possible prescribing cascade: {index} → fluid retention → {marker}

title: Possible prescribing cascade: {index} → cough → {marker}
plain: Blood-pressure medicines ending in “-pril” (ACE inhibitors) can lead to a dry, tickly cough that cough medicines do not help.
clinician: ACE-inhibitor cough is a labeled adverse reaction; antitussive starts after ACEI initiation exceed starts before (Vegter 2010).

title: Possible prescribing cascade: {index} → bladder leakage → {marker}
plain: Memory medicines such as donepezil can lead to bladder leakage, and bladder medicines started for it can work against the memory medicine.
clinician: Cholinesterase inhibitor users are more likely to start a bladder antimuscarinic (Gill 2005); the combination has opposing mechanisms and adds anticholinergic burden.
